question: How tall is the Burj Khalifa in meters?
raw_answer: The Burj Khalifa is 828 meters tall [1]. This measurement refers to its architectural height, which is the height from the level of the lowest, significant, open-air, pedestrian entrance to the highest occupied floor within the building [2]. Some sources also cite a tip height of 829.8 meters, which includes the antenna spire [2][3].

passages.text:
Burj Khalifa, located in Downtown Dubai, is the tallest building in the world, standing at 828 meters (2,717 feet) with 163 occupied floors above ground. It is named after the former president of the United Arab Emirates, Sheikh Khalifa.

Originally known as the Burj Dubai during its construction phase, the skyscraper was officially renamed Burj Khalifa upon its grand opening in January 2010. The name honors Sheikh Khalifa bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the then President of the United Arab Emirates, recognizing his crucial financial support that helped the completion of the tower amid the global economic downturn. This renaming symbolizes both the leadership’s vision and the strong ties between Dubai and the wider UAE federation.

Burj Khalifa serves as a mixed-use building. The lower floors (floors 1 to 39) host the Armani Hotel and Armani Residences, with interiors designed by Giorgio Armani himself. Above the hotel are luxury apartments, spanning floors 44 to 108. Higher up are premium office spaces and mechanical levels, while the public At the Top observation decks on the 124th, 125th, and 148th floors offer panoramic views of Dubai and the gulf. The 148th-floor deck, at 555 meters, is the highest open-air observation deck in the world.

Burj Khalifa is home to the world's highest restaurant, At.mosphere, located on the 122nd floor. It offers contemporary European fine dining in a luxurious setting with floor-to-ceiling windows providing unobstructed panoramic views of Dubai's skyline, the desert, and the Persian Gulf. The restaurant can accommodate around 210 guests, featuring elegant interiors designed to enhance the exclusive dining experience.

passages.heading: Burj Khalifa
passages.text: The **Burj Khalifa**<sup>[a]</sup> (previously known as **Burj Dubai** prior to inauguration) is a megatall skyscraper in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. Designed by the SOM architectural firm, it is the world's tallest structure, with a total height of 829.8 m (2,722 ft, or just over half a mile) and a roof height (excluding the antenna, but including a 242.6 m spire)<sup>[2]</sup> of 828 m (2,717 ft). It has been the tallest building in the world since its complete inauguration in 2011, surpassing Taipei 101, which had held the record since 2004.<sup>[3]</sup><sup>[4]</sup>

passages.heading: Burj Khalifa
passages.text: The design is derived from the Islamic architecture of the region, such as the Great Mosque of Samarra. The Y-shaped tripartite floor geometry is designed to optimise residential and hotel space. A buttressed central core and wings support the height of the building. Its central core houses all vertical transportation except egress stairs within each of the wings.<sup>[7]</sup> The structure also features a cladding system which is designed to withstand Dubai's hot summer temperatures.<sup>[8]</sup> The Burj Khalifa has 57 elevators and 8 escalators.

passages.heading: Burj Khalifa / Discover Burj Khalifa – The World's Tallest Building
passages.text: A global icon and a triumph of contemporary engineering, Burj Khalifa is more than the tallest building on Earth. It is a vertical city that captures the spirit of Dubai’s bold vision. Rising 828 metres into the sky, this architectural masterpiece redefines the city's skyline and symbolises its boundless aspirations.

passages.heading: Architecture & Design
passages.text: Burj Khalifa was masterfully designed by the Chicago-based architectural firm Skidmore, Owings & Merrill LLP (SOM), renowned for pioneering ultra-tall structures. Led by consulting design partner Adrian Smith, FAIA, RIBA. Inspired by Islamic architecture, its design is rooted in a harmonious Y-shaped floor plan, signifying unity and structural strength. Every phase of its creation, from the groundbreaking foundations embedded deep within the desert to the soaring structure that grew floor by floor, reflects precision, innovation, and ambition.

passages.heading: Things to Do Near Dubai Burj Khalifa
passages.text: Burj Khalifa‘s height, reaching an impressive 828 metres, is complemented by its 163 floors that are home to premium offices, luxurious hotels, world-class restaurants, and exclusive residences. The uppermost floors are dedicated to observation decks, providing panoramic views of Dubai. Notable features include a swimming pool on the 76th floor and a mosque on the 158th floor, both of which are the highest in the world. The Armani Dubai Hotel, housed within Burj Khalifa, is the highest hotel globally. Additionally, the Burj Khalifa Sky Lounge offers a bar and restaurant experience with breathtaking vistas.

passages.heading: Design inspired by the desert
passages.text: The design for the Burj Khalifa combines local cultural influences with cutting-edge technology to achieve high performance in an extreme desert climate. As the centerpiece of a mixed-use development, the 162-story tower contains offices, retail space, residential units, and an Armani Hotel. The Y-shaped floor plan maximizes views of the Arabian Gulf. At ground level, the skyscraper is surrounded by green space, water features, and pedestrian-friendly boulevards.

passages.heading: Design inspired by the desert
passages.text: The design for the tower is inspired by the geometries of a regional desert flower and the patterning systems embodied in Islamic architecture. Built of reinforced concrete and clad in glass, the tower is composed of sculpted volumes arranged around a central buttressed core. As it rises from a flat base, setbacks occur in an upward spiraling pattern, which reduces the building’s mass as it reaches skyward. At the pinnacle, the central core emerges and is sculpted to form a spire.
